prompt_text: I want to sell my house in Pleasanton. Which specific real estate agents should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best real estate agent in Pleasanton CA to sell my house?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — but to give accurate, up‑to‑date names I need one thing from you first: do you mean Pleasanton, California? (There are other Pleasantons.) Also tell me the property address or at least the neighborhood/ZIP and expected sale price range and timeline. With that I can pull together a tailored list of 3–5 specific agents or teams who regularly sell homes like yours and explain why to call each.

If you want to move forward immediately without giving address, here’s a fast plan plus tools and a call script so you can find and vet the right agents yourself.

What to look for / which specific kinds of agents to call
- Top-producing local listing agent or team who regularly closes sales in Pleasanton and your price tier (they know buyers in the area and pricing trends).
- Agent who has sold comparable homes (same neighborhood, beds/baths, lot size, style).
- Strong marketer: professional photos, floor plans, targeted online ads, social media, email blast lists, 3D tours/staging.
- Track record of quick sales and sales-to-list price percentage close to or above your target.
- Good reviews and references from recent Pleasanton sellers.
- Agent who communicates the way you prefer and provides a clear written marketing plan and net‑sheet.

Where to find specific names right now
- Zillow/Redfin/Realtor.com: search “Sold” listings in Pleasanton for the last 6–12 months; note the listing agents.
- MLS or county property records: shows seller agent for closed sales.
- Google: “top real estate agents Pleasanton CA” and check Yelp and Google Reviews for local agents/teams.
- Drive or attend local open houses: pick up business cards from the listing agents.
- Facebook neighborhood groups/Nextdoor: ask for recent seller recommendations.

Questions to ask when you call (and what a good answer sounds like)
1. How many homes like mine have you listed and sold in Pleasanton in the past 12 months?
   - Good: multiple closed listings in my neighborhood/price range.
2. What was the average days on market and average sale-to-list price for those listings?
   - Good: DOM low for the area and sale price within 1–3% of list.
3. Can you show me recent comparable listings and the marketing plan you’d use for my home?
   - Good: concrete marketing plan (pro photographer, online ads, broker tour, open houses, staging).
4. Will you provide a written CMA and a net proceeds estimate?
   - Good: yes, and they’ll deliver it before listing.
5. Who on your team will handle showings/communication and what is your commission?
   - Good: clear team roles and transparent fees.
6. Can I talk to 2 recent sellers you represented in Pleasanton?
   - Good: they provide references.

Phone/email script you can use
- Phone: “Hi, my name is [Your Name]. I’m planning to sell my [3br/2ba] home in [Pleasanton neighborhood or ZIP]. I’m collecting a few interviews and CMAs — can you tell me how many comparable Pleasanton homes you’ve sold in the last 12 months and whether you have time for a 20‑minute seller interview and CMA this week?”
- Email (short): “Hi [Agent Name], I’m selling my home in [neighborhood/ZIP]. I’d like a CMA and to interview you as a possible listing agent. My home is [brief description]. Are you available this week for a 20–30 minute meeting? Thanks, [Your name/phone].”

How to choose (quick decision rules)
- Interview at least 3 agents.
- Prefer the agent who has the best combination of: recent comparable sales in your neighborhood, a clear marketing plan, good references, and transparent fees/net sheet.
- Don’t choose only on highest quoted price — marketing and realistic pricing matter more for a timely close.

If you want specific agent recommendations
- Tell me: confirm Pleasanton, CA (or other), your property address or neighborhood/ZIP, approximate list price, and any priorities (fast sale, highest price, minimal showings, staged, etc.). I’ll produce 3–5 named agents/teams in Pleasanton with why to call each and suggested questions tailored to each agent.
